newsitem.title: USA: Raytheon sees earnings on target, minus charge.
newsitem.headline: Raytheon sees earnings on target, minus charge.

text.p: Electronics and defence equipment firm Raytheon Co. said Friday it expected its third quarter operating income to fall 15 percent from the year-earlier level, sparking a sharp drop in its stock.
Raytheon's stock fell $4 to $49 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Raytheon said operating income would fall because of delays in awards and contracts at its engineering and construction division and because of slow sales of major home applicances.

The company's engineering and construction division, Raytheon Engineers & Contructors, is expected to report a third quarter operating loss of $8 million as a result of a strike at its plant in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, said company Chief Financial Officer Peter D'Angelo.
D'Angelo said the strike has ended and "the operation should return to profitability in the fourth quarter."
The company makes electronics, defence equipment, small aircraft, and Amana, Caloric and Speed Queen appliances.

Raytheon said its net income per share was expected to meet analysts' expectations, as tax credits for research and development and interest income should offset the expected shortfall in operating income. According to First Call, analysts expect Raytheon to report third quarter income of 89 cents a share.
Raytheon earned $354 million, or 82 cents per share adjusted for a stock split, in the third quarter of 1995.
The company previously announced it would take a special charge of 9 cents a share to close a plant in Delaware, Ohio.

The company said delays in engineering and construction awards and weakness in the appliance sector will also affect its fourth quarter. However, Raytheon said it expects earnings per share for the year to exceed last year's.
The company earned $787 million, or $3.23 a share, in 1995.
